stances.claim: The social media have come of age in our country -- Facebook and Twitter's awesome people-gathering power has been proven beyond doubt by the Million People March (Aug 26 2013). Significantly, traditional media (Inquirer, major radio-TV networks) expanded MPM's span/breadth/depth to reach masses without computers/tablets/smartphones. Numbers no longer matter -- what matters is that its message has penetrated and outraged all sectors via mass media.

MPM was different from Edsa PP1 (Marcos ouster) and PP2 (Estrada ouster), which had a common major convenor (Cardinal Sin) and led to instant ouster of top leaders after 4 days of continuous rallies. In contrast, MPM was spontaneously called by an enraged populace to galvanize action against a bedeviling issue of governance (pork barrel) -- not to oust a sitting President or renew religious fervor or propel candidacies. It had no big-name convenor, no institutional organizer, no platform speakers, no grandstanding orators, no pre-planned program, no busses to ferry hakot, no financiers, no celebrity singers, no rabble rousers -- yet came the mammoth crowd that vented rage by simply being there, sensed common cause, and shooed away pretenders and fellow travelers with different agenda.

Unlike PP1 and PP2, which ousted two sitting chief executives after 4 days of continuous Edsa rallies, MPM gathered only for a day and did not produce any immediate palpable result. Nonetheless, P-Noy, SP Drilon, Speaker Belmonte, and other leaders heard the people's cry. Even before the rally, P-Noy announced the demise of PDAF. While the 2014 budget still retains pork (with Abad's safeguards), CJP forecasts that given P-Noy's reformist streak, pork would be eventually abolished within the next three years. The people have spoken and P-Noy is not deaf.

MPM is destined to transform not just our leaders but the very culture and mores of our political and social life -- and that cannot be rushed, lest it disembowels and destroys the very foundations of society that it seeks to strengthen and uphold.

Social media are the newest species of the freedom of expression and are entitled to the same constitutional protection (Art III Sec 4). Free expression originated in the Middle Ages with people speaking against kings/emperors → followed by right to peaceful assembly to redress grievances → printing press expanded it to freedom of the press → Industrial Age added labor's right to strike and picket → radio/TV/cinema were given constitutional mantle → opinion polls and election surveys became parts of free expression in the last two decades. Twitter, Facebook, and other social media are the most recent technological expansion. Government may as well adjust to the new vigilance of our citizenry.

What better way to demonstrate this recognition and adjustment than to be more transparent and accountable -- the best guarantee being the FOI bill. Let's abolish pork, investigate and penalize the pork abusers and plunderers, and make sure this mess never happens again through a new FOI law guaranteeing greater public scrutiny.

notable_anecdotes: The MPM-vs-EdsaPP-contrast inventory -- 'no big-name convenor, no institutional organizer, no platform speakers, no grandstanding orators, no pre-planned program, no busses to ferry in the hakot, no financiers to feed them, no celebrity singers to entertain them and no rabble rousers to taunt them' -- among the most concentrated 'what-MPM-was-not' enumerations, used to characterize the rally's unprecedented self-organization.

The 'numbers no longer matter' framing -- explicitly bypassing the one-million / 400,000 / 50,000 attendance debate to focus on message-penetration via mass media -- a sharp interpretive move acknowledging then-current attendance controversies.
The pretenders-and-fellow-travelers-shooed-away detail -- the crowd's self-discipline in rejecting agenda-hijackers -- a rare CJP observation of crowd-as-organic-curator-of-its-own-message.

The free-expression-evolution chronology (Middle Ages → peaceful assembly → printing press → press → labor strike/picket → radio/TV/cinema → opinion polls/election surveys → social media) -- CJP's tightest historical-expansion narrative of Art III Sec 4 protection-scope.

The 'social media originally used for bonding with friends and relatives, they have become new tools of social transformation and reformation' framing -- concise capture of the Facebook/Twitter functional-evolution from social to political.

The 'cannot be rushed, lest it disembowels and destroys the very foundations of society' warning -- CJP's most striking image for slow-revolution caution, with the unusually visceral 'disembowels' verb choice.
P-Noy's pre-rally PDAF-demise announcement -- captured as evidence that the leaders heard the cry even before the rally, a procedural-pre-emption that softened MPM's apparent immediate impact.

The triple-imperative closing -- 'Let's abolish pork, let's investigate and penalize the pork abusers and plunderers -- and let's make sure this mess will never happen again through a new FOI law' -- among CJP's most condensed FOI-as-prevention closing-calls, tied directly to the three-banishment-needs framework of A446.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban marks the coming of age of Philippine social media with the Million People March of Aug 26 2013 -- Facebook and Twitter's awesome people-gathering power proven beyond doubt. Traditional media (Inquirer, major radio-TV networks) expanded MPM's span/breadth/depth to reach masses without computers/tablets/smartphones, so that numbers (one million? 400,000? 50,000?) no longer matter -- what matters is that its message penetrated and outraged all sectors. MPM was different from Edsa PP1 (Marcos ouster) and PP2 (Estrada ouster): both had a common major convenor (the late Jaime Cardinal Sin) and led to the instant ouster of top leaders. True, the Catholic Church (World Youth Day), Bro. Mike Velarde, and Iglesia ni Cristo have convened larger Luneta congregations, but these were well-planned religious liturgies; electoral 'miting de avance' and political campaigns have drawn bigger crowds. In contrast, MPM was spontaneously called by an enraged populace to galvanize action against a bedeviling issue of governance -- not to oust a sitting President, renew religious fervor, or propel candidacies. It had no big-name convenor, no institutional organizer, no platform speakers, no grandstanding orators, no pre-planned program, no busses to ferry in the hakot, no financiers, no celebrity singers, no rabble rousers -- yet came the mammoth crowd that vented rage by simply being there, sensed common cause and fervor, and shooed away pretenders and fellow travelers with different agenda. Unlike PP1 and PP2 which ousted chief executives after 4 days of continuous Edsa rallies, MPM gathered only for a day and produced no immediate palpable result. Nonetheless, P-Noy, SP Drilon, Speaker Belmonte, and other leaders heard the cry -- in fact, even before the rally, P-Noy announced PDAF's demise. The 2014 budget still has pork with Budget Sec Butch Abad's safeguards, but given P-Noy's reformist streak, CJP forecasts pork's eventual abolition within the next three years. The people have spoken and P-Noy is not deaf. The abolition will be gradual -- unlike Marcos's and Estrada's ousters -- and MPM is destined to transform not just our leaders but the very culture and mores of our political and social life. That cannot be rushed, lest it disembowels and destroys the very foundations of society that it seeks to strengthen and uphold. Social media are the newest species of the freedom of expression and are entitled to the same Art III Sec 4 constitutional protection -- 'No law shall be passed abridging the freedom of speech, of expression, or of the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and petition the Government for redress of grievances.' Free expression originated in the Middle Ages with people speaking against kings and emperors → followed by the right to peaceful assembly to redress grievances → expanded by the printing press to freedom of the press → joined in the Industrial Age by labor's right to strike and picket → followed by radio, TV, and cinema under constitutional mantle → joined in the last two decades by opinion polls and election surveys. Twitter, Facebook, and other social media are the most recent technological expansion. Originally used for bonding with friends and relatives, they have become new tools of social transformation and reformation. Now that the people have found these novel tools, they will continue to use them -- government may as well adjust to the new vigilance of citizenry. The best way to demonstrate that recognition is greater transparency and accountability, with the FOI bill as the best guarantee. Let's abolish pork, let's investigate and penalize the pork abusers and plunderers -- and let's make sure this mess will never happen again through a new FOI law guaranteeing greater public scrutiny.
